words.ex: Good teachers imbue their students with a love of learning.

words.def: using more words than are needed
words.ex: His verbose answer took ten minutes just to say yes.

words.def: different from what is normal or expected
words.ex: The scientist rechecked the anomalous result.

words.def: a long, angry speech criticizing something
words.ex: The coach went on a tirade about sloppy passing.

words.def: freedom from punishment or harm
words.ex: No one should be able to break the rules with impunity.

words.def: able to work successfully
words.ex: Solar panels are a viable way to power the cabin.

words.def: very sad and without hope
words.ex: After losing his dog, Marco was despondent for weeks.

words.def: very poor and in need
words.ex: The clinic gives free care to indigent families.

words.def: to say something openly and firmly
words.ex: The new members avow their loyalty to the club.

words.def: a story in which characters and events stand for bigger ideas
words.ex: The fable about the ants and the grasshopper is an allegory about hard work.

words.def: a speech in a play in which a character speaks their thoughts aloud while alone
words.ex: In her soliloquy, the queen reveals her secret plan to the audience.

words.def: shocking and vivid in a way meant to grab attention
words.ex: The magazine printed lurid stories to sell more copies.

words.def: a long-standing rival or enemy that is hard to defeat
words.ex: The team from across the river has been our nemesis for years.

words.def: a release of strong emotions that leaves a person feeling relieved
words.ex: Crying at the end of the sad movie gave Priya a sense of catharsis.

words.def: great happiness
words.ex: The family wished all their guests health and felicity in the new year.

words.def: the social surroundings a person lives in
words.ex: The artist grew up in a milieu of musicians and painters.

words.def: an economic system in which a nation builds wealth by exporting more than it imports, often using colonies
words.ex: Under mercantilism, colonies were expected to send raw materials to the home country.

words.def: a phrase that joins two opposite words, like 'jumbo shrimp'
words.ex: 'Deafening silence' is an oxymoron.

words.def: not thinking about the future; short-sighted
words.ex: Spending all your savings on candy is a myopic choice.

words.def: to try to win someone's favor, especially by flattering them
words.ex: The new student tried to ingratiate himself with the teacher by bringing apples.

words.def: the official ending of a law, system or practice, especially slavery
words.ex: Many activists worked for decades for the abolition of slavery.

words.def: something placed in a time period where it does not belong
words.ex: A wristwatch on a knight in the movie was an obvious anachronism.

words.def: so surprised and confused that you do not know how to react
words.ex: The teacher was nonplussed when the whole class handed in blank pages.

words.def: a member of the highest, most privileged social class
words.ex: The aristocrat lived in a palace with hundreds of servants.

words.def: used in casual, everyday conversation rather than formal writing
words.ex: The novel's dialogue is colloquial, full of slang and short phrases.
